castAddBody.text:
one mental model: 

robot vacuums don't clean as well as a focused human, 

but they do better than a tired or distracted human.

they spend more time cleaning, with slightly worse results

but they free humans to do things other than cleaning

SAME THING WITH DISHWASHERS

maybe coding agents *should* work the same way--

produce some mediocre output

which **was always good enough**

but for the human need to carve out professionalism

and distinguish exceptional quality

which allows individuals to stake their right to some reward

taken from a finite resource

or allocation of a fixed budget

in a world of scarcity, good enough is not good enough

but in a world of abundance, is good enough good enough?

like in Hawaii nobody ever worries about dressing for the weather

slippahs are good enough

but in New York, you need 5 different pairs of shoes
